besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses ('Die Son is 'n ster' / 'elke ster maak sy eie lig').
besluite.rede: Both clauses have their own subject and verb, so the AWS 2017 comma is required and nothing else changes.

besluite.fout: 'weer ... terugbons' is pleonastic: 'terug' already says the light comes back.
besluite.rede: Dropping the redundant 'weer' carries no information away, leaves the protected 'Ons sien hulle omdat' intact and brings the sentence in line with the definition of weerkaats.

besluite.fout: 'geen lig van sy eie nie' follows English 'no light of its own' and reads stiffly.
besluite.rede: The proposal is natural Afrikaans, says the same thing, repeats the lesson's own phrasing 'nie sy eie lig maak nie', and 'hom' in the next sentence still points to the wall.
The original is an ordinary, clear Afrikaans phrase; the proposal is longer and adds a transitive 'n flits skyn', which copies English 'shine a torch'.
The first part is an imperative with no subject of its own, and 'Kyk ... en jy sien' works as one unit, so the house AWS rule does not ask for a comma here.

besluite.fout: 'hoë land' as an uncountable phrase is loose and wooden beside 'berge'.
besluite.rede: 'hooglande' is the natural Afrikaans word for the same high-lying land, a Grade 6 reader knows it, and it touches no protected word ('vlaktes' stays).
